data.name: Jagmohin
data.gender_notes: Jagmohin is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from Sanskrit words 'Jagat' meaning world and 'Mohin' meaning conqueror. The name Jagmohin carries the meaning “World Conqueror” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Jagmohin usually hope their child will grow to embody world conqueror and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents one who has conquered their inner world, symbolizing enlightenment and self-realization.
data.etymology: Jagmohin belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “World Conqueror.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jagmohin total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Jagmohin holds a significant place in Hindu culture, signifying a powerful and victorious individual who has the ability to conquer the material world. It evokes a sense of strength, courage, and determination, reflecting the values and characteristics that are deeply ingrained in Hindu traditions and beliefs.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Jagmohin represents the triumph of the soul over worldly desires and attachments. It symbolizes the inner struggle and eventual victory in the quest for self-realization and enlightenment, aligning with the themes of Hindu spirituality and the ultimate goal of attaining moksha or liberation from the cycle of birth and death.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Jagmohin: Radiant Lord. A name evoking the inner light of the soul, inspiring the individual to illuminate their inner Self and shine brightly, like the sun, in the world.

vedic_reference.note: A name of Lord Vishnu, found in the Vedas and other Hindu scriptures

historical_references.reference: Jagmohin was a powerful Rajput king of the Chauhan dynasty, who ruled the region around Alwar in present-day Rajasthan, India, during the late 12th and early 13th centuries.

Jagmohin is also mentioned in the epic poem 'Prithviraj Raso' as one of Prithviraj Chauhan's bravest warriors. He joined the battle against Muhammad Ghori's invasion of India in 1192 AD and is known for his exceptional valor and loyalty.
